body:
I'll leave it like this for now, it doesn't hurt. We also have something similar in `ustring.cpp`:
```
#ifdef _MSC_VER
#define _CRT_SECURE_NO_WARNINGS // to disable build-time warning which suggested to use strcpy_s instead strcpy
#endif

#if defined(MINGW_ENABLED) || defined(_MSC_VER)
#define snprintf _snprintf_s
#endif
```

This is probably worth cleaning up, I would assume in 2026 there should exist standard cross-platform APIs for that. From a quick search, it seems `snprintf` was non-standard for VS < 2015 but it should be good to use now instead of `strcpy` (and we don't seem to use `strcpy` anymore in `ustring.cpp` anyway).

So we could also use `snprintf` here instead of `strcpy`.

Anyway that's outside the scope of this PR and something that could be reviewed codebase wide to remove some of this old tech debt.

> Do you recall why you added all this logic for !GLAD_ENABLED on Linux/Wayland?

Not sure, but that's why I preserved as much history as possible :P

Since it seems to come straight from the Wayland PR, I dug a bit through its log and its commit history. It looks like  we originally linked directly to glvnd, and thus didn't have GLAD enabled at all:

https://github.com/deralmas/godot/blob/90a71d2008c7a48543d44d6325675305803e96a5/platform/linuxbsd/detect.py#L214-L217

https://github.com/deralmas/godot/blob/90a71d2008c7a48543d44d6325675305803e96a5/drivers/gl_context/SCsub#L5-L26

https://github.com/deralmas/godot/commit/90a71d2008c7a48543d44d6325675305803e96a5

> That said, while I tried to touch the least amount of "outside code" as
possible, I had to disable temporarily the GL debugging code for non
GLAD-powered platforms (which already assumed GLAD quite a lot), with
the consequence of disabling it for the whole `linuxbsd` platform **since
the Wayland `DisplayServer` doesn't make use of it and would thus not
compile properly.**

(emphasis mine)

Actually I was sure that there was still an option to directly link to lib(E)GL, but I can't find proof of that. If the assumption is that we can always use GLAD then I guess we can indeed get rid of all that extra logic.

Man it's been *a while*
